title: add-stratified-sequence-fusion-benchmark-and-kernel-sampler-reporter
author: Tara O'Neill
release_notes: Adds a new stratified sequence fusion benchmark harness and a kernel-sampler reporter for fine-grained per-kernel latency attribution. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Production inference workloads show correlated sequence patterns that cause fragile kernel hotpaths when multiple sequence-length cohorts are multiplexed on the same GPU. Existing bench harnesses in benchmark-lab either sweep single sequence mixes or run coarse multimodal mixes; we lacked a tool that both (a) stratifies requests by length+prefix archetype and (b) fuses those cohorts into deterministic fused-batches to exercise kernel selection heuristics. This PR introduces the 'stratified sequence fusion benchmark' (ssf-bench) plus a 'kernel sampler reporter' that samples kernel execution timing and attributes to sequence cohorts, enabling more precise regressions and kernel-level heatmaps.

What changed (high level): added new ssf benchmark runner, input population generator with archetype catalog, fusion scheduler that builds fused-batches respecting KV cache priming, and a reporting pipeline that aggregates per-kernel latencies back to cohort keys and fusion shapes. Added unit tests, an integration harness that runs the bench on a small GPU CI target (cpu-mode fallback available), and a visualization shim that emits ndjson reporter artifacts compatible with our existing flamegraph pipeline. Also included docs and a short recipe for reproducing divergent kernel selection cases locally.

Design notes and tradeoffs: The fusion scheduler intentionally biases fused-batch composition to preserve KV cache locality and to produce deterministic fused shapes for reproducible profiling. This increases the synthetic realism at the expense of requiring archetype definitions; archetypes can be generated from our session-sampler export or hand-curated for targeted cases. Sampling is probabilistic: the kernel-sampler emits 1% of kernels by default (configurable) to avoid overwhelming CI runs and storage. We validate sampled attribution by checking that sampled kernel ids appear in end-to-end traces during flamegraph debug runs.

Runtime and integration: The runner supports a cpu fallback mode for CI which mocks kernel timings; real GPU runs are intended for perf lab. The reporter emits ndjson lines with the following fields: timestamp, job_id, fusion_shape, cohort_key, kernel_id, kernel_ms_mean, kernel_ms_p50, kernel_ms_p95, sample_count. Artifact files are small (compressed) for typical runs and integrate with existing artifact collectors.

Review conversation (highlights):

- Miguel Santos: "CI bench-smoke failed on first run due to resource constraints in the docker image (missing nvidia libs for the gpu-mode smoke test). Recommend making gpu-mode skip on CI images without NV present and mark tests accordingly."
- Author (Tara): "Updated ci/bench-smoke.yml to detect /dev/nvidia0 and skip gpu-mode; fixed tests to run in cpu fallback by default on CI. Re-ran CI."
- Liang Chen: "Can we get a quick flamegraph sample in artifacts to show kernel hotspot mapping? Otherwise looks good."
- Author (Tara): "Added a small sample artifact (bench/ssf/sample-artifacts/ssf-small-flame.ndjson) and referenced it in the PR description so reviewers can eyeball mapping."
- Asha Patel: "Approving after small nits addressed (docs phrasing)."

CI summary: initial run: bench-smoke (cpu-mode) failed due to missing vendor libs; rerun after changes passed. Unit tests: all green. Lint: minor pyflakes nits fixed on follow-up commit. End-to-end bench job (manual) produced expected kernel attribution heatmap in our perf visualization tooling.

Metrics and expected outcomes: In early runs the ssf-bench highlighted a previously unnoticed kernel choice regression in the attention kernel selection when a 128+512 fusion occurred; after this PR we used the reporter to verify a kernel-fallback mitigation patch reduced the p95 per-kernel latency by ~18% on our T4 perf lab cluster for the target workload mix.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged on 2026-02-20 after approvals and CI green. Follow-ups: (1) add an ops playbook to automate nightly ssf runs against canary kernels (ENG-3810), (2) probe sampling rates and retention policy for artifacts in long-running experiments.

How to run locally (short): python bench/ssf/runner.py --config examples/ssf/local-run.yml --mode gpu --output /tmp/ssf-out --sample-rate 0.01. See docs/benchmark-lab/ssf-runbook.md for full guidance and archetype derivation.
